The timeslice that follows each timeslice

Source: R/navigate.R
calendar_next.Rd

The successor chain at a timeframe: for every timeslice, the one that comes next. Used wherever a quantity is carried from one slice into the next — a storage level, a ramping limit — and by order-constrained clustering.

Usage

calendar_next(x, timeframe = NULL, within = NULL, wrap = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A Calendar.

timeframe

Timeframe whose timeslices are chained. Defaults to the finest.

within

Optional coarser timeframe whose boundaries the chain stays inside: the successor of the last slice of a day is the first slice of that same day, not of the next one. NULL (default) chains the whole timeframe as one sequence, and "ANNUAL" says the same thing explicitly – the root is the whole year, so a chain confined to it is not confined at all.

wrap

TRUE (default) closes each chain into a cycle, so the last slice's successor is the first of its group. FALSE gives NA there, leaving the sequence open.

Value

A data.frame with one row per timeslice at timeframe, in chronological order: timeslice and next_timeslice, both qualified node ids as calendar_timeslices() with qualified = TRUE returns them. With wrap = FALSE, next_timeslice is NA on the last row of each group.

Details

A cycle is the default because an energy-system calendar represents a typical period rather than a one-off interval: a storage level that must return to where it started makes the period repeatable, and an open chain lets the model empty the store for free on the last slice.

Grouping under within uses each node's whole path, not its label, so a calendar whose hour labels repeat under every day chains each day separately rather than pooling the twenty-four labels into one group.

See also

calendar_children(), calendar_timeslices()

Examples

cal <- calendar("d365_h24")
head(calendar_next(cal))                             # all 8760, cyclic
#>   timeslice next_timeslice
#> 1  d001_h00       d001_h01
#> 2  d001_h01       d001_h02
#> 3  d001_h02       d001_h03
#> 4  d001_h03       d001_h04
#> 5  d001_h04       d001_h05
#> 6  d001_h05       d001_h06
head(calendar_next(cal, within = "YDAY"))            # 365 cycles of 24
#>   timeslice next_timeslice
#> 1  d001_h00       d001_h01
#> 2  d001_h01       d001_h02
#> 3  d001_h02       d001_h03
#> 4  d001_h03       d001_h04
#> 5  d001_h04       d001_h05
#> 6  d001_h05       d001_h06
head(calendar_next(cal, within = "YDAY", wrap = FALSE))
#>   timeslice next_timeslice
#> 1  d001_h00       d001_h01
#> 2  d001_h01       d001_h02
#> 3  d001_h02       d001_h03
#> 4  d001_h03       d001_h04
#> 5  d001_h04       d001_h05
#> 6  d001_h05       d001_h06
